issues.description: Every supplied run path depends on missing raw site or site-survey files. The datasheet says the proprietary underlying data cannot be shared because the research-site NDA prohibits sharing; reproduction therefore requires a separately authorized controlled-access arrangement. The package does not establish that such access is available.

The first tldmain.dta save uses a closed keep list after duplicates drop project_id. That list omits manager_ID and year required by the later ManagerData merge, and omits team_perf and project_size used by the table code. The later reload and overwrite cannot restore fields already dropped. The intended project-level row construction, required retained fields, and key uniqueness must be confirmed against authorized data before any source edit.

The ildmain.dta keep list omits up_eval, peer_eval, and other_eval, while Table 1 Panel C reloads ildmain.dta and uses those fields. The later ildmain overwrite only derives averages and turnover_t1 from fields already saved. Confirm whether Panel C should use the available 360eval intermediate or whether the individual keep list should retain these ratings; the intended sample and unit must be preserved.

Table 2 loads tldmain.dta but requests H_Relationship and V_Relationship, introduced in the separate dynamic-survey branch and present in tdsmain after its matched project_id merge. Confirm whether Table 2 is intended to use the matched tdsmain sample or another construction before changing the input or merge sequence.

evidence.description: Author datasheet states that raw data are proprietary and the research-site NDA prohibits sharing the underlying data.
evidence.quote:
While the raw data is proprietary, the authors provide any non-proprietary portion of the code. All
codes and the list of identifiers used in the analyses have been submitted to the journal editors.
Note that any company-specific terminology has been modified to protect the confidentiality of
the company. The underlying data cannot be shared as the authors signed a non-disclosure
agreement with the research site that prohibits any sharing of the data.

evidence.description: Online appendix describes the Workplace Survey as a same-site employee/supervisor survey distributed using Qualtrics and states that anonymity precludes linking responses to the observational data.
evidence.quote:
The surveys were circulated via the online web-based survey tool Qualtrics. We sent the online
survey links to our contact at the field site. The site then distributed the links to all the supervisors
and employees via its internal communication system. The surveys were launched on October 8,
2022, and closed on November 7, 2022.

Confidentiality

In distributing the survey, we guaranteed anonymity to the participants in order to protect the
identity of respondents and elicit truthful responses. Thus, no identifying information was
collected as part of the survey. Maintaining anonymity is also in compliance with IRB guidelines.
While the anonymity prevents us as researchers from linking the workplace survey data with the
original observational data, we decided to preserve the anonymity of survey participants to allow
for eliciting truthful survey responses.

evidence.description: The program reloads ildmain, derives averages and forward turnover_t1, and overwrites ildmain.dta.
Table 1 Panel C reloads ildmain.dta and reads up_eval, peer_eval, and other_eval after deriving rating comparisons.
evidence.quote:
use "CCS_UI in Teams/JAR data/ildmain.dta", clear
		univar perf_eval_score_annual Tenure age turnover_t1
		preserve 
		duplicates drop ID, force
		univar UI female
		restore 
			
	//Panel C: 360-Degree Person Evaluation Ratings
	foreach var of varlist up_eval peer_eval other_eval{
		gen `var'_2d = int(`var'*100)/100 //round ratings to 2 significant digits 
	}
		
	gen high_supervisor = 1 if up_eval_2d > other_eval_2d | up_eval_2d > peer_eval_2d
		replace  high_supervisor = 0 if mi(high_supervisor)
		
	gen high_peer = 1 if peer_eval_2d > up_eval_2d
		replace  high_peer = 0 if mi(high_peer)
		
	gen high_other = 1 if other_eval_2d > up_eval_2d
		replace  high_other = 0 if mi(high_other)

	gen equal_up_peer = 1 if up_eval_2d == peer_eval_2d
		replace equal_up_peer = 0 if mi(equal_up_peer)
		
	gen equal_up_other = 1 if up_eval_2d == other_eval_2d
		replace equal_up_other = 0 if mi(equal_up_other)
			
	preserve 
	duplicates drop ID, force
	univar up_eval_2d peer_eval_2d other_eval_2d high_supervisor high_peer high_other equal_up_peer equal_up_other

gen p_UI_60_80 = 1 if p_UI > 0.60 & p_UI <= 0.80 & !mi(p_UI)

dependency_review.description: 360Data.dta is generated from the required 360Data.xls input and then read for cleaning to create the evaluation intermediate.
TeamData.dta is imported from TeamData.xlsx, then read and merged with 360eval.dta by ID/year before team-level variables are derived.

tldmain.dta is first saved from the team panel and later reloaded, merged with ManagerData.dta, and overwritten. The closed first keep list drops fields required by that merge and later table consumers; see I_TLD_HANDOFF.
tdsmain.dta is created by joining Team Survey ID.xls to Team Dynamic Survey Data.dta on jyd_id, then merged with tldmain.dta by project_id using matched rows and overwritten.
Survey_employee.dta is produced by the employee survey cleanup and is read as the master dataset for the employee/supervisor append.
Workplace Survey.dta is generated by appending employee and supervisor survey intermediates, then read for survey construction that saves wpsmain.dta.
ildmain.dta is first saved from the individual panel, then reloaded and overwritten with derived fields. Its saved schema lacks the three ratings Table 1 Panel C later uses; see I_ILD_RATINGS.
wpsmain.dta is generated from the cleaned Workplace Survey data and later reloaded for the workplace-survey analyses including Table 8.

actions.description: Obtain an explicitly authorized route for the research-site archival data and employee/supervisor Workplace Survey response files under the NDA, or document that controlled access is unavailable. The public appendix instrument does not provide response data.
steps: Request the research site's permitted controlled-access method and the author-held data dictionary for each raw workbook, crosswalk, and Qualtrics response export.
Confirm that access covers all seven files read by the supplied program and the required matching keys, retained periods, and survey response columns.
Stage authorized inputs under the relative CCS_UI in Teams/raw data/ path in a separate working copy; retain the package source bytes unchanged.
validation: After authorization, verify each file's format, column names, identifiers, row units, period, and mapping to the supplied import and merge calls with bounded metadata checks.
Do not link anonymous Workplace Survey response records to the archival panel; the appendix says respondents were kept unidentifiable.

actions.description: Install or activate a Stata-compatible user-written univar command in the runtime's user ADO path before the full workflow is attempted.
steps: In a separately authorized software-setup step, install a compatible release of the Stata univar command in the host Stata user ADO path; do not replace the author's univar calls with another statistic command.
validation: Before data execution, use Stata metadata only to confirm which univar resolves to the intended ado file and record the command version.

actions.description: Ask the authors to confirm the intended tldmain unit, retained fields, and merge keys before any change to the closed keep list.
steps: Confirm whether one row per project_id is intended and whether manager_ID and year are constant at that unit.
Confirm the intended source and construction for team_perf and project_size and which fields must survive the first tldmain save.
validation: After authorized data access, compare the confirmed keys and fields with bounded metadata from the intermediate files before editing or running dependent tables.

actions.description: Ask the authors to identify the intended source and sample for the ratings used in Table 1 Panel C before changing the individual-panel keep list or table input.
steps: Confirm whether Panel C should read the ratings from 360eval.dta or whether up_eval, peer_eval, and other_eval should be retained in ildmain.dta.
Confirm the intended observational unit and sample for the reported rating comparisons.
validation: After authorized data access and author clarification, verify the selected source contains the required rating fields and intended identifiers before any edit or execution.

actions.description: Ask the authors to confirm the intended Table 2 relationship-variable source and sample before changing its input file or merge sequence.
steps: Confirm whether Table 2 is intended to use tdsmain.dta after the matched project_id merge, or a different relationship-variable construction.
validation: Compare the confirmed intended sample with the available project_id coverage after access is authorized; do not infer a source change from filenames alone.

actions.description: After authorized access, install/activate the verified software prerequisite, and resolve the documented intermediate handoff questions, run the supplied entry program in a separate relative-path working copy in its authored order.
steps: Use a separate working copy with the CCS_UI in Teams directory beneath the Stata working directory so the program's relative raw-data and JAR data paths resolve; keep frozen package and audit-generation bytes unchanged.

Stage all seven authorized inputs under CCS_UI in Teams/raw data/: 360Data.xls, TeamData.xlsx, ManagerData.xls, Team Dynamic Survey Data.xls, Team Survey ID.xls, Qualtrics_Workplace Survey_Employees.csv, and Qualtrics_Workplace Survey_Supervisors.csv.

Run the authored 360Data import and cleaning to create 360Data.dta and 360eval.dta; import TeamData.xlsx to TeamData.dta, merge with 360eval.dta by ID/year, derive team variables, and save the initial tldmain and ildmain intermediates.
Import ManagerData.xls to ManagerData.dta, reload tldmain, apply the authored manager_ID/year merge and manager-derived fields, and overwrite tldmain after the handoff fields and unit are confirmed.
Import and rename the team-dynamics workbook, join it to Team Survey ID.xls on jyd_id to create tdsmain, then merge matched project_id rows with tldmain and overwrite tdsmain.

Clean the employee and supervisor Qualtrics exports to their authored Stata intermediates, append them into Workplace Survey.dta, apply the authored filtering, recodes, and PCA steps, and save wpsmain.dta.
Reload ildmain, derive the authored averages and turnover_t1, and overwrite ildmain after resolving the missing-rating handoff.

Run the supplied main analysis and figure code in authored order after resolving the Table 2 relationship-variable sample question; keep the Stata session continuous where the program relies on data in memory.
validation: Before any run, confirm site authorization covers all seven inputs, the exact column/key expectations, and the anonymous survey-linkage constraint; confirm univar resolves to the intended compatible ado.

During an authorized run, retain the generated intermediates and record the exact producer and consumer outcomes; validate that each intended key, row unit, and required variable survives before dependent analyses.
Do not claim reproduction until the generated outputs and author-confirmed handoffs have been checked against the stated analysis targets.

review_notes: Static package review and bounded metadata checks cover the supplied Stata entry program, author datasheet and appendix, all 15 frozen dependency IDs, the packaged identifier workbook probe, the assigned resource catalog, and registered Stata metadata. The full supplied code path depends on seven missing site inputs barred from sharing by the stated NDA; controlled access remains unconfirmed. No compatible local/public input product was established in the bounded catalog queries, which is not evidence of absence or permanent denial. Stata 18 and required estimation helpers are available; univar is a preparation item. The generated review records the complete dependency set and the produced-intermediate lineage. Three code handoff issues remain for author/data confirmation: the tldmain keep list, the ildmain rating fields, and Table 2's dynamic-survey source/sample. The online appendix also describes analyses without supplied code; those analyses are outside the supplied executable closure. The separate author log was not used as local feasibility evidence. The qfitci standalone lookup and failed Stata manual open are unreferenced process-only captures; official StataCorp evidence supports qfitci as a Stata 18 plot type, and the set memory statement is not a blocker. No scientific program, author startup file, data payload, or model was executed.
